title: Interleaved reservoir and kernel-matchmaking for paged-attention KV reuse and prefill prioritization
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: For workloads with long context tails and mixed sequence-length traffic we see suboptimal KV residency and decode tail spikes. The current prefill logic evicts at page granularity using simple recency heuristics and the kernel selector does not account for upcoming prefill cost, resulting in frequent re-prefills and higher p99 decode latency. Goal: design an interleaved allocation/eviction strategy (shadow reservoir) and a kernel-matchmaking score that jointly optimizes for reuse probability, prefill cost, and kernel affinity. Integrate that into prefill scheduling so prefill work is prioritized for pages whose reuse probability and kernel-match score exceed thresholds, and evict low-value pages proactively during idle windows.
acceptance_criteria: p95 decode latency for mixed workloads improves by >= 12% in cluster benchmark
prefill-related repeated fetches per minute reduced by >= 40% on representative tenant traces
no regression in median generation latency for short-sequence requests
end-to-end canary rollout with traffic-split shows stable CPU/GPU utilization and no increased OOM incidents
implementation covered by unit + integration tests and an e2e microbenchmark; design doc reviewed by runtime and infra leads
design_decisions: Introduce a lightweight shadow-reservoir per GPU with generational buckets (hot/warm/cold) that stores compacted touch metadata rather than full page contents to track reuse without increasing residency pressure

Score pages by combined metric: reuse_score = alpha * predicted_reuse + beta * kernel_affinity - gamma * prefill_cost. Kernel_affinity measures how well a page co-locates with kernels that minimize decode overhead (memory access patterns, fused attention variants).
Prefill scheduler will prioritize pages above dynamic threshold and schedule lower-priority prefill work only during underutilized time-slices (cooperative decode throttling).

Eviction policy becomes reservoir-aware: remove cold pages with low reuse_score first, but allow short-term soft-reserve for pages recently used by constrained tenants to avoid repeated prefill storms.
Keep admission simple: new pages initially enter warm bucket; promotion to hot requires repeated hits within a sliding window to avoid hoarding by adversarial workloads.
implementation_notes: Prototype shadow-reservoir as 128B metadata entries per page (touch_count, last_touch_ts, last_kernel_id, estimated_reuse_prob)
Add kernel_match component to runtime kernel registry that exposes a per-page affinity score computed from model architecture + token distribution heuristics
Integrate prefill priority queue with soft-deadlines; prefill tasks annotated with reuse_score and estimated token-cost to allow batching decisions downstream
Instrumentation: add counters for prefill_retries, page_promotions, prefill_latency_breakdown (io, kernel-prefill, scheduling_wait)
Fall-back: if any component fails, revert to LRU eviction and default kernel selector to ensure safety
tests_and_metrics: Run mixed trace microbench (short chat bursts + long context streaming) and measure p50/p95/p99 decode latency, GPU utilization, and prefill_retries per-minute
A/B canary with 1% traffic using enhanced scheduler vs baseline for 48 hours; check tail latency and error rates
Synthetic adversarial workload to ensure promotion thresholds prevent starvation of other tenants
Unit tests for scoring math, and simulated unit that replays traces against reservoir to verify eviction decisions match expected policies
rollout_plan: Stage 1: deploy shadow-reservoir read-only + telemetry in runtime-1.20-alpha to gather signals (no eviction changes) - 2 weeks
Stage 2: enable scoring + prefill-priority in canary (1% tenants), kernel-matchmaking off for safety - 1 week
Stage 3: enable kernel-matchmaking + reservoir-based eviction for canary (1%) - monitor 48h
Stage 4: progressive ramp to 25% then 100% with automated rollback thresholds on p99 latency or OOMs
Stage 5: post-rollout retro and perf baseline update
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: scoring miscalibration causes eviction of pages with true long-term value. Mitigation: conservative default alpha/beta/gamma and shadow-read telemetry before enforcement.
Risk: increased CPU for scoring/maintenance; Mitigation: offload heavy computations to maintenance threads and amortize scoring with sampling windows.
Risk: adversarial tenants manipulate touch patterns to reserve space. Mitigation: admission control with promotion quotas and tenant-weighted decay.
Risk: interactions with existing kernel prefill batching producing worse latency; Mitigation: add integration tests and stage kernel-matchmaking opt-in flags.
